implementation_notes: The completion protocol is built into the framework: the producer calls CompleteAdding() after the last item, consumers iterate queue.GetConsumingEnumerable() (or check IsCompleted), and the enumeration ends once the remaining items are drained - no reserved value travels through the collection, so no payload can collide with the pill. For async pipelines use System.Threading.Channels and ChannelWriter.Complete(), which marks the channel complete and lets await foreach finish after the buffered items. A hand-rolled sentinel is only justified for a third-party queue without a completion API, or when an orderly stop must be distinguishable from normal completion (shutdown versus fault).
pitfalls: After CompleteAdding(), Add/TryAdd throw InvalidOperationException and Take() on an empty completed collection throws too - use GetConsumingEnumerable or IsCompleted, never an IsCompleted-plus-Take race.
Forgetting CompleteAdding() leaves every consumer blocked in MoveNext/Take forever; GetConsumingEnumerable has no timeout.
ChannelWriter.Complete(error) surfaces the error as ChannelClosedException in every reader - passing an exception turns the shutdown into a fault, so use Complete() for an orderly stop.
BlockingCollection blocks thread-pool threads; for async consumers prefer Channels rather than mixing blocking collection waits into async code.
